identify: Confirm the item is a transformer or wound magnetic component before dismantling.
Look for a laminated or ferrite core with insulated windings and leads.
Separate unusually large, sealed, leaking, burned, or unknown units for manual review.

workflow.title: Isolate
workflow.instruction: Disconnect the unit from equipment and verify it is not connected to stored electrical energy.

workflow.title: Inspect
workflow.instruction: Check the core, winding access, fasteners, resin/potting, and whether dismantling can be done without excessive labor.

workflow.title: Compare whole-unit value
workflow.instruction: Record the sell-whole value before dismantling so Recovery Lab can compare it with expected separated value.

workflow.title: Open mechanically
workflow.instruction: Use appropriate hand tools and guards to expose accessible windings without burning insulation or using chemical stripping.

workflow.title: Separate fractions
workflow.instruction: Sort copper-bearing windings, steel/ferrite core material, aluminum if present, and nonmetal residue into separate containers.

workflow.title: Verify winding metal
workflow.instruction: Do not assume every winding is copper. Verify copper-colored material beneath insulation before assigning copper value.

workflow.title: Time-value check
workflow.instruction: Enter recovered value and labor minutes into Worth My Time? and compare against selling the transformer whole.
